title: Cross-validate: roundtrip parity
description: Cross-platform roundtrip validation. DONE - shared vectors
notes:
2026-08-25 roundtrip parity blocker: Python focused frame/vector/schema suite passes (240 passed, 10 skipped); Rust spec frame parse+roundtrip tests pass (2) and shared vector consumer passes (8), including every signed address mode and signed max payload. Read-only ctypes exercise of existing C lichen_frame_parse/write over current test/vectors/link_frame.json and link_frame_signed_modes.json: all 9 unsigned positives roundtrip exact; signed_encrypted rejects -EPROTONOSUPPORT and unsigned 256-byte over-max rejects -EMSGSIZE; but every modern signed positive (broadcast, short, extended, elided, and all max-payload variants: 9 total) rejects -EINVAL, so no signed parity. Root cause: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/frame.c:19/76-85 treats LLSec bit 7 as reserved and parses no 8-byte signer identifier; write path frame.c:139-142/183-190 forbids signer and keeps bit 7 clear. The current profile requires S and SI together and carries signer EUI-64. Existing clean C test passes only because lichen/tests/frame/main.c:334-383 hardcodes stale 0x20/0x21 signed frames without signer while labeling them current link_frame.json; current vectors use 0xA0/0xA1 and are 8 bytes longer. C production/header are current-phase read-only, so cannot close until C frame struct/parser/writer adopt SI/signing layout and the C test consumes current fixed corpus including signed max and negative categories.
2026-08-26 re-audit: blocker remains unchanged. Python live frame + signed-mode consumers: 135 passed, 10 skipped. Rust lichen-link shared_vectors: 4 passed. Fresh standalone C frame test builds/passes 1/1, but it embeds obsolete 0x20/0x21 signed frames without signer EUI-64. Read-only ctypes against the live C lichen_frame_parse and all current positive canonical vectors: unsigned 9/9 accepted; signed 0/9 accepted, every broadcast/short/extended/elided signed and signed-max vector returns -EINVAL. Exact production gap: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/frame.c defines bit 7 as LLSEC_RESERVED, rejects it at lines 74-77, clears signer state at 84-85, and lichen_frame_write forbids signer state at 139-143 and leaves bit 7 clear at 182-190; link.h lines 206-208 still document signer IID as not carried/reserved. Current vectors require S+SI and an 8-byte signer EUI-64. Cannot close until C parser/writer/header and its vector consumer adopt the current layout. No source edits made.
2026-08-27 canonical parity recheck: Python frame parser/vector subset passed 103 with 10 expected skips (2 unrelated LinkLayer/SchcSessionManager fixture tests deliberately deselected); Rust lichen-link shared_vectors passed 4/4. Zephyr remains signed-incompatible: the established direct C corpus run accepts/roundtrips all 9 unsigned positives but accepts 0/9 modern signed positives, because current frame.c rejects bit7 and omits the required 8-byte signer EUI-64. Host C self-tests pass only their obsolete 0x20/0x21 signed fixtures. No dirty frame files touched. Added direct blocking dependencies on Zephyr frame parse/serialize project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.1.4.3 and Zephyr SenderID project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.1.5.4.3; no duplicate edges existed.
